subject: Linguistics
title: Tense and Aspect
description: A quick, practical guide to Tense and Aspect.

hook.text: 'I ate' vs. 'I was eating'—both are past tense, but they frame the event differently.

buildup.text: Tense locates an event in time; aspect describes its internal structure—completed, ongoing, or repeated.

discovery.text: English marks aspect with auxiliaries: 'has eaten' (perfect) vs 'is eating' (progressive).

twist.text: Mandarin has no tense marking—particles like 'le' and 'zhe' mark aspect instead.

climax.text: Tense and aspect interact to create a rich timeline that sentences can zoom in or out of.

punchline.text: When it happened is tense; how it unfolded is aspect.

quiz.question: What does aspect describe?
options: The internal structure of an event
